stories.headline: US soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
body: UK police arrested a 41-year-old US military member near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia.
Counterterrorism police worked with the FBI and US military.
He is accused under the National Security Act.
stories.vc: Spy cases raise defence security costs across NATO.

stories.headline: US skips UN human rights review for a second year
body: The US left its seat empty at a UN human rights review for the second year running.
It is the only member state ever to do so.
Every country is meant to be reviewed every four to five years.
stories.vc: Stepping back from UN processes can weaken US influence in global rule-making.

stories.headline: UN peacekeepers come under fire in southern Lebanon
body: UNIFIL says about a dozen rounds were fired at one of its patrols near Tyre.
The patrol returned fire; no one was hurt.
It called for an investigation.
stories.vc: Instability in Lebanon weighs on regional trade and tourism.

stories.headline: InMobi buys naming rights to a Bengaluru metro station
body: InMobi paid ₹65 crore to name Bengaluru's Ibbaluru Metro Station for 30 years.
It will be called InMobi Ibbaluru Metro Station.
InMobi is working towards an IPO in India.
stories.vc: Naming deals give Namma Metro extra non-fare income.

stories.headline: NMDC in talks to invest in Russian lithium
body: State-run miner NMDC is in early talks with Russia's Rosatom on lithium projects, sources say.
India wants secure lithium supplies for batteries and EVs.
Talks remain preliminary.
stories.vc: Securing lithium abroad supports India's EV and battery plans.

stories.headline: SoftBank gains on Lenskart and Meesho, loses on Ola Electric
body: SoftBank's Vision Fund 2 booked $394 million of gains on Lenskart and Meesho last quarter.
It booked a $42 million loss on Ola Electric.
Delhivery and FirstCry also lost value.
stories.vc: Mixed results for listed startups show investors are picking winners carefully.

stories.headline: Proximal Ventures raises $27.5M to back AI drug-development tools
body: Former SignalFire investor Sahir Raoof raised $27.5 million for his first fund.
It backs startups using AI in drug development services.
First-time funds face one of the toughest markets in years.
stories.vc: AI tools for pharma are a growing niche for specialist investors.
